title: 50x single-thread speedup vs reference at n=36
description:
Measure single-thread `permanent_bipedal3` (SIMD path, T13) against `permanent_mod3_reference` (T8) at $n=36$ on the dev host; the speedup must be $\ge 50\times$.

## Background

This is the headline perf claim of the epic (CLAUDE.md success criterion 3 + the epic's success criterion 3). The in-tree reference (T8 — faithful Julia port) provides the per-machine baseline; the SIMD-dispatched bipedal3 path (T13) is the contender. The criterion is `[hard]` because a per-machine in-tree baseline exists (T8 measures itself on the same hardware that runs T13).

The aspirational comparison vs the paper's published Julia number on a Zen 4/5 host is `[aspirational]` because the paper's hardware is different and the Julia toolchain version drifts.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] Dedicated S1 Criterion benchmark at `crates/gf2-algebra/benches/s1_n36_speedup.rs` runs `permanent_mod3_reference` AND `permanent_bipedal3` (SIMD path) at $n \in \{24, 28, 32, 36\}$ with the same seeded inputs. T10's bench (`benches/permanent.rs`) remains the fast-tier sweep; this dedicated bench isolates the long-running n=36 cells so default `cargo bench` is not slowed.
- [ ] [hard] Measured speedup $\frac{T_{\text{reference}}}{T_{\text{bipedal3-simd}}} \ge 50$ at $n=36$ on the dev host (AMD Ryzen 9 5900X).
- [ ] [hard] CSV at `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/s1_speedup-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` records mean wall-clock and ratio at $n \in \{24, 28, 32, 36\}$ for both implementations.
- [ ] [hard] Hardware fingerprint and seed are recorded in the CSV header.
- [ ] [hard] Writeup at `dev/plans/s1_speedup_results.md` exists, attached via `jit doc add`.
- [ ] [aspirational] Same comparison vs the paper's published Julia number ($86.9\times$ from a 4.20 GHz desktop) — comparable speedup at $n=36$ would mean $\ge 50\times$ vs a Zen 4/5 reference Julia run.
- [ ] [hard] `criterion-1.5x` gate passes (the SIMD path is at least 1.5× faster than the previous baseline; satisfied at n=24/28 where the bench fits the gate runtime).

## Amendment history (2026-05-12)

- Criterion 1 amended from "Criterion benchmark in T10 includes ..." to "Dedicated S1 Criterion benchmark at `benches/s1_n36_speedup.rs` ...". T10's bench explicitly dropped n=32 and n=36 from the bipedal sweep (see `crates/gf2-algebra/benches/permanent.rs:5-12`); single-cell n=36 ref runtime is ~150 s/sample, so Criterion's min sample_size=10 puts one cell at ~25 min wall-clock. Isolating that into a dedicated bench keeps T10's default `cargo bench` budget intact and matches the project's slow-tier philosophy.
